direct_or_reviewed.confidence_boundary: Catalog binding / bounded lexical evidence / reviewed effect scope are retained separately; execution is unverified.

contract.review_scope: Full retained body read, authored input/output/effect/branch/configuration/error/transaction/concurrency explanations; source current per owner.
contract.purpose: Create an immediate cycle-count plan and return its identity.
inputs_defaults: Captured declaration; placeholders are not executable argument values: CREATE PROCEDURE CCP_InsertCCPlan( @iGroupSize numeric(9), @stWhs nvarchar(25), @stUserName nvarchar(30), @iPlanNum numeric(9) output) AS
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: No explicit validation of group size, warehouse or user. Target type, NULL, key and foreign-key rules apply. The output is assigned only after the insertion reaches its success path.
output_shape: One OUTPUT parameter @iPlanNum receives scope_identity(); no row result. NOCOUNT ON is set.

ordered_branches.explanation: Insert one plan with current UTC created/stamp time, caller group size and warehouse, NULL MASTER_NAME, IN_CREATION=N, RELEASED=Y, and all three totals zero.
After checking the INSERT error, assign scope_identity() to the numeric(9) OUTPUT plan number. This creates a plan row; it creates no count request or work instruction.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Initializes plan counters and fixed creation/release flags without inventory changes.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: Caller supplies group size and warehouse; flags are coded values rather than effective configuration reads.
error_and_return_handling: Immediately detected INSERT error returns -1; no TRY/CATCH or rollback exists.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, savepoint or SET XACT_ABORT in this body. Caller/session transaction behavior governs partial completion; this contract does not assume atomic child calls.
concurrency: The identity is scope-local. There is no duplicate-plan existence check, so separate calls can create separate plans.
contract.trigger_behavior: No captured DML trigger is attached to the direct persistent target tables. Transitive child effects are not inferred.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application callers, current record state and active permissions were not observed. No extension, assembly or Azure-function changes are required by this documentation task.
Explicit child/function calls are listed; their exact source contracts bound transitive effects. Opaque selectors are retained as technical evidence, without fabricated labels.

evidence.description: Complete retained definition reviewed with individual behavioral notes; private original hash/redaction parity verified.

global_limits: Source-backed explanations describe the current captured replica. They do not diagnose an unseen work unit, container or user session.
No operational data, procedure execution or application configuration changes were performed. Caller actions, effective settings and whole-process duration remain evidence-specific.
Opaque literals are not exposed. Source identifiers and technical edge cases are supporting evidence, not instructions to execute SQL.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
Owner backup/leftover and item-master-failure suggestions are hypotheses. Name patterns and missing references do not validate them. No deletion recommendation is made.
